relations.statement: Each of the five single-system import predicates is independent of the others: the countermodel for import i fails i, while every other import j (j ≠ i) is admitted by that countermodel.
relations.hypotheses: i ranges over SingleSystemImport; this is a rational finite countermodel check and not Gleason at n >= 3.

lemmas.statement: Finite certificate shell for QM_204-C0: redundant normalization is separated from uniqueness by the five-import mutual independence countermodels. This is not a discharge of Born uniqueness.
lemmas.lean_skeleton:
theorem qm204_c0_shell (i : SingleSystemImport) : ¬ AdmitsImport (countermodelFor i) i := by
  exact (FiniteQM.five_import_mutual_independence i).1

near_misses.claim: Five-import mutual independence proves Born-rule uniqueness (Gleason) for n >= 3.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The theorem only separates five rational import predicates by countermodels; it does not establish a uniqueness statement for measures on dimension n >= 3.
